title: Saul, head and shoulders taller (1 Samuel 9–10)
hook: the first king is chosen, hiding among the baggage

segments.voice: Yesterday, a boy in the night at Shiloh, learning to say speak, Lord. Your line was thy servant heareth. Who did you listen to all the way to the end? Day three hundred ninety-nine, the end of week fifty-seven.

A farmer's donkeys have wandered off. He sends his son and a servant to find them. They search the hill country for three days. Nothing. They're about to give up and go home when the servant says: there's a man of God in the next town. Maybe he can tell us where the donkeys went. So a tall young man walks into town looking for lost animals, and walks out a king. The man of God is Samuel, now grown old. The tall young man is Saul. The Bible says there was no goodlier person among the children of Israel, and that from his shoulders upward he stood above everyone.
screen: `THE LOST DONKEYS.` → `ASK THE MAN OF GOD.` → `LOOKING FOR ANIMALS, FOUND A CROWN.`

segments.voice: First, the backstory. Israel had asked Samuel for a king, to be like the nations around them, and the text treats that as a sad request: they're setting aside God as their king. God tells Samuel to give them one anyway. Then Samuel meets Saul, and before Saul can even ask about the donkeys, Samuel tells him: they're found, stop worrying. Then, privately, he takes a little vial of oil, pours it on Saul's head, and kisses him. The Lord has anointed you prince over his people. Anointed: in Hebrew, mashiach, the word English borrows as Messiah; Greek translates it Christ. Here, at its start, it's simply oil on a nervous young man's head. And Saul is nervous. When Samuel first hints at greatness, Saul answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "Am not I a son of Jemini of the least tribe of Israel?" Benjamin, the smallest tribe. Then comes the public choosing. All Israel gathers, lots are cast, tribe by tribe, family by family, and the lot falls on Saul. Everyone turns to look, and he isn't there. They ask the Lord where he is, and in the Hebrew the answer is: he has hidden himself among the baggage. The Douay-Rheims, following the Latin, says only: "Behold he is hidden at home." Either way, the man who stands taller than everyone is crouched out of sight. They pull him out, he stands head and shoulders above them, and the people shout: "God save the king." It's a tender, almost funny beginning, and the story will darken: Saul's reign ends in jealousy and tragedy. But this week has been full of people who felt too small: Gideon in the winepress, Ruth the stranger, Hannah in tears, a boy in the dark. Saul makes one more.
screen: `ISRAEL ASKS FOR A KING.` · `OIL ON HIS HEAD: ANOINTED.` · `THE LEAST TRIBE OF ISRAEL.` · `HIDING AMONG THE BAGGAGE.` · then, large: `GOD SAVE THE KING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice where you hide. Settle, and breathe. Saul hid behind the luggage at the exact moment he was called. Ask yourself where your luggage is. Busyness. Jokes. Your phone. Saying I'm not the right person. Letting someone louder go first. Don't judge it. Just notice one place you duck out of sight when you're being asked to stand up. Then picture stepping out, the way Saul finally did, and standing where people can see you. If you pray, you can ask for that courage. The bell holds the time.
Saul. Israel's first king, tall and frightened, anointed with oil by Samuel and found hiding among the baggage on the day he was chosen. Today's word.

Your line: hiding in the baggage. Today, step out once where you'd usually hide. And that's week fifty-seven: Gideon's fleece, Samson, Ruth on the road, gleaning, Hannah's prayer, speak, Lord, and Saul. Day three hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: Catholics hear the story of Saul's anointing in the weekday Mass readings, and the Church's own anointings, at baptism, confirmation and ordination with sacred chrism, carry on the old sign of oil poured on someone chosen.

original.note: Hebrew: anointed. Samuel pours oil on Saul's head; the word comes into English as Messiah, and into Greek as Christ.

trapdoor: what you thought: Saul was a proud, tall king.
what it means: he starts out looking for lost donkeys, calls his tribe the least in Israel, and hides among the baggage on the day he's chosen.
what a scholar hears: the Douay has 'hidden at home' where the Hebrew and the King James have 'among the stuff'; and the anointing gives us mashiach, Messiah.
